intended_object: The canonical A-algebra isomorphism Cℓ(A ⊗_R V, Q_A) ≅ A ⊗_R Cℓ(V, Q): taking the Clifford algebra commutes with base change (generalising the complexification of real Clifford algebras). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The definition bundles `toBaseChange` and `ofBaseChange`, which are mutually inverse A-algebra maps, into an `AlgEquiv` between `CliffordAlgebra (Q.baseChange A)` and `A ⊗[R] CliffordAlgebra Q`. That is exactly the standard isomorphism. R can be any commutative ring, A any commutative R-algebra and V any R-module. The only extra hypothesis is `Invertible (2 : R)`. It is required because Mathlib's `QuadraticForm.baseChange` is built from `QuadraticForm.tmul`, which is only defined when 2 is invertible. The file `QuadraticForm/TensorProduct.lean` notes this explicitly: its uniqueness lemma `baseChange_ext` holds without the assumption, "unlike `QuadraticForm.baseChange`". The isomorphism does hold over any commutative ring in the literature, but its statement needs the base-changed form, and Mathlib has no more general construction of it. So the restriction comes from the setting the statement needs, not from the definition being too narrow. No more general Mathlib counterpart exists.
